# Cribrum - v2.2.0

**More evidence. Clearer decisions. A review workflow that keeps you moving.**

LibreBugBounty 2.2.0 brings **Cribrum**, the local response classifier, into the
heart of the workspace. Stored responses become explainable findings, multiple
claims stay visible from triage to report export, and the redesigned Review
lets you work through a queue with more room for the evidence and less waiting.

Everything runs in your own workspace. You stay in charge of the assessment.

## Meet Cribrum

Cribrum reads HTTP/DOM observations already retained by browser work. Versioned
rules, exact evidence spans and explanations show what it found and why, without
another target request during normal classification. SQL diagnostics, disclosed
queries, file-include errors, runtime failures, reflected input and protection
pages can be considered together instead of disappearing behind a single label.

The release ships **engine 1.3.8**, including corrections for native database
diagnostics, serialized and multiline response carriers, PHQL parser errors and
request values carried in URL paths. It keeps observed errors, suspected
vulnerabilities and confirmed findings separate. A database error is not proof
of SQL injection; reflected input is not proof of XSS execution. SQLi, LFI and
RFI are not automatically confirmed.

Multiple claims now carry their certainty, evidence and immutable decision
history through Review, inventory filters, saved views, statistics and exports.
Choose which findings to adopt before confirming a case. Rejecting an unsuitable
proposal records the decision for that case and puts the originating rule into
human review, without disabling the rule for other cases.

The explicitly selectable **behavior-triage 1.5.2 candidate pack** provides the
registered SQL, file-include, reflection and context/disclosure/WAF detectors.
Existing core and private packs remain the default. Candidate selection starts
in shadow mode; active evaluation needs separate opt-in. Installing this release
does not activate a candidate or reclassify the inventory.

## Review built for long sessions

- **Give the screenshot the space it deserves.** The normal view has a larger
  evidence area, collapsible queue information and details, and a clearer bottom
  bar: compact website information, room for the findings, decisions on the right.
- **Focus mode gets out of the way.** A compact menu replaces the stack of
  floating buttons. Website information sits above the decision keys; image
  information sits with zoom and fit at the bottom right. Review information
  opens to the right when space permits, with a responsive fallback for smaller
  windows.
- **Stay on the keyboard.** **F** toggles focus, **M** opens its menu, **I** toggles
  details, and **H** hides or shows the controls. Bindings remain configurable;
  mouse and touch work too. Pills, spacing and expanded panels have been checked
  in German and English, at desktop, half-window, phone and landscape sizes.
- **Keep reviewing while saves finish.** Up to **five upcoming cards and
  screenshots** preload quietly. When the next card is ready, your decision is
  queued and the review advances. Saves run one at a time in the background,
  using the choices captured for each case, with a visible pending count.
- **Recover without guessing.** A failed save leaves the case open and shows a
  recovery notice. An unconfirmed response is reported without silently retrying
  the decision. Back, Skip and Defer synchronize with pending saves; leaving the
  page warns while writes are outstanding. If a preview is unavailable, the
  ordinary save-and-advance path remains available.

The default DDEV setup now uses **two screenshot workers and two recheck
workers**, reducing concurrent browser work while retaining parallel processing.

## From evidence to a report you can explain

Versioned report projections bind qualified evidence to its source and current
PoC. Combined cases retain their additional findings and original certainty;
missing or stale evidence and WAF review holds stay visible. Private HTTP
artifacts remain outside reports unless explicitly selected. Report eligibility
does not send a disclosure or replace your review.

Local diagnostics and offline reclassification explain retained results while
preserving manual decisions and history. A separate source-reading ledger records
who inspected which source and request context, with expiring reservations for
parallel work. A reading receipt does not confirm a vulnerability.

There are everyday fixes too: Intake keeps duplicate receipts and their
existing-case links after reload, exact repeated URL pastes no longer append a
second copy when automatic submission is off, and backup/storage tools provide
clearer retention and upgrade checks. PHP 8.4 is supported alongside PHP 8.3.
The locked Symfony dependencies have also been updated to address known security
advisories.

## Help make Cribrum sharper

**Cribrum has been exercised extensively, and it still gets some things wrong.**
It can miss a useful signal, match a misleading error message or need context
that a stored response cannot provide. This release does not claim perfect
detection or a measured universal accuracy rate. Review the evidence, especially
before treating a suggestion as a reportable vulnerability.

**Found a miss? An over-eager match? Have a better regex? Please contribute.**

- [Report a bug or detection gap](https://github.com/grassmann-it/librebugbounty/issues/new).
  Include the engine/rulepack version, expected result, actual result and a small
  sanitized or synthetic reproducer. False positives and false negatives are
  equally useful.
- [Contribute a rule or detector improvement](https://github.com/grassmann-it/librebugbounty/blob/v2.2.0/docs/cribrum/contributing.md).
  Regex fixes, new diagnostic signatures, parsing corrections and better
  explanations are welcome. Include a positive example, a close negative example
  and an offline regression test so the improvement stays fixed.
- Start with the [Cribrum guide, contracts and examples](https://github.com/grassmann-it/librebugbounty/blob/v2.2.0/docs/cribrum/README.md).
  Detection changes belong in the reviewed rule/detector paths; candidate packs
  remain shadow-first. You do not need a finished patch to report a useful case.

Please keep private target URLs, captured secrets, credentials and personal data
out of public issues and pull requests. Synthetic fixtures that preserve the
relevant syntax and input relationship are ideal.

## Upgrade

Create and verify a [database and artifact backup](https://github.com/grassmann-it/librebugbounty/blob/v2.2.0/BACKUP.md),
then follow the [upgrade guide](https://github.com/grassmann-it/librebugbounty/blob/v2.2.0/README.md#upgrade-an-existing-workspace).
Upgrade the application and workers together, run the additive migrations and
reload open browser pages. Keep the database, evidence and private rulepacks
from the same workspace.

Alongside the claim/observation and report-evidence schemas, this release adds
the source-reading ledger and queued-assessment receipts. Existing case URLs,
manual decisions and artifact references are retained; no database reset is
required. Candidate activation remains a separate, explicit choice.
